l6xst3: With **gustar**, the thing that is liked decides the verb. One thing or an action (infinitive): **gusta**. Several things: **gustan**. _Me **gusta** el café_, _Me **gusta** cocinar_, _Me **gustan** las plantas_.
cepuou: The person who has the taste goes in the pronoun in front: **me** (yo), **te** (tú), **le** (él, ella, usted), **nos** (nosotros), **os** (vosotros), **les** (ellos, ellas, ustedes). To say the name: _**A** Mario **le** gusta el fútbol_.
3k703q: For general tastes, the noun takes the **article**: _Me gusta **la** música_, _No me gustan **los** gatos_. And to make it negative, **no** goes before the pronoun: _**No me** gusta madrugar_.
1g86koc: With _gustar_ the person goes in the pronoun **me**, and _montañas_ is plural: **gustan**.
1cq837x: **Encantar** works like gustar, but it's stronger: _Me **encanta** el mar_, _Me **encantan** los perezosos_. Don't say _me encanta mucho_: encantar already means a lot.
1wm9wj3: A useful scale: **me encanta** > **me gusta mucho** > **me gusta** > **no me gusta mucho** > **no me gusta nada**.
zfzaj7: To react to what someone else says: if you agree, **a mí también** (positive sentence) or **a mí tampoco** (negative sentence). If not, **a mí no** or **a mí sí**. _—Me gusta el frío. —¡**A mí no**!_
sun03w: Para mí, contigo: pronouns after a preposition
awnsrn: After a preposition (**para, de, sin, a, con**…), almost all pronouns are the same as the subject: _para **él**_, _de **ella**_, _sin **nosotros**_, _con **ustedes**_. Only two change: yo → **mí** and tú → **ti**.
18ujx2n: With **con** there are two special forms, written as one word: **conmigo** (con + yo) and **contigo** (con + tú). Never _con mí_ or _con ti_.
nbzsbe: Watch the accent: **mí** (pronoun: _para mí_) has an accent; **mi** (possessive: _mi casa_) doesn't. **Ti** never has an accent. That's why you say _**A mí** me gusta_: it's the preposition _a_ + **mí**.
16xnd5n: Trick: if you can swap the word for _él_ (_para él_), it's the pronoun **mí**, with an accent. If you can swap it for _su_ (_su casa_), it's the possessive **mi**.

189p9xa: **Prepositions** and **al / del** to say where: _Vivo **en** San Pedro, cerca **de la** universidad_, _Voy **al** trabajo **en** bus_. **Adverbs**: _El piso está **muy** cerca_, _Me gusta **mucho**_.

a7xw0v: Gusta or gustan: the final n, and a stressed mí
1c6nvmu: Between **gusta** and **gustan** there's only one sound: the final **n**. It's short, but it changes the meaning: _me gusta el libro_ / _me gustan los libros_. Listen to what comes next too: _los_, _las_ and the plural **s** confirm there are several things.
18jl44b: **Mí** (pronoun) is a **strong** word: it has its own stress. _A **mí** me gusta_, _para **mí**_. On the other hand, **mi** (possessive) is weak and joins the noun: _mi-ca-sa_.
ayskk5: In **conmigo** and **contigo**, the stress is on the second syllable: _con-**mi**-go_, _con-**ti**-go_.
12vkxfl: **Mí** with an accent is a pronoun (_para mí_); **mi** without an accent is a possessive (_mi casa_). **Ti** never has an accent. **Conmigo** and **contigo** are written as one word.
d2c30p: _Pa-ra-TI_: short and clear, with no accent when written.
